886:
Fees for collection of garbage and yard waste shall be those as established by resolution of the city council, and shall be published in the office of the city hall where utility bills may be paid.
(Code 1989, § 11-65; Ord. No. 187, § 14, 9-20-1982; Ord. No. 314, § 4, 10-12-1992)
887:
(a) With respect to residential and commercial and industrial consumers receiving bills from the city, fees shall be paid on or before 20 days after the billing statement is mailed from the city. With respect to fees billed directly from the contractor, such shall be paid as required by the contractor.
(b) Any fees not paid on time and falling into a delinquent status shall have a penalty imposed thereon. Such penalty rate shall be published in the office of the city hall where utility bills may be paid and be in accordance with the then current resolution as may be adopted from time to time by the city council.
(c) The payment of such fees shall be delinquent 20 days after the bill for such fees has been mailed. The collection of delinquent fees for garbage and yard waste collection shall be the same as for the collection of delinquent taxes.
(Code 1989, § 11-66; Ord. No. 187, § 15, 9-20-1982; Ord. No. 277, § 1F, 7-23-1990; Ord. No. 314, § 4, 10-12-1992)
888:
(a) In accordance with this chapter, the tenant, occupant, or proprietor of any place from which garbage or rubbish accumulates shall be charged for the services of collection, removal and disposal of such garbage and rubbish at the rates established or approved by the city council.
(b) All county unified school districts requiring refuse collection from the public schools shall be upon such terms and conditions as they are mutually agreed upon or considered as a special collection point.
(c) The city council, by resolution, may set or approve a flat monthly rate for removal from a business establishment of extra materials such as waste paper, wooden boxes and the like.
(Code 1989, § 11-67; Ord. No. 187, § 19, 9-20-1982)
889:
For the removal of rubbish and periodic accumulation of excess garbage and yard waste, the price to be charged for collection, removal, and disposal shall be quoted in advance, and shall be based upon the amount of material to be removed, as well as upon the time involved and the loading thereof. Such price shall be determined by the prevailing cost for providing the requested service.
(Code 1989, § 11-68; Ord. No. 187, § 20, 9-20-1982)
890:
(a) If any charges herein provided for are paid in advance and garbage and yard waste collection service is discontinued or cancelled prior to the end of the period for which the charges are paid, a refund shall be made at that portion of the charges which is for the period subsequent to the discontinuance or cancellation of such service; provided, however, that no refund of less than one month's charge for garbage and yard waste collection service shall be made.
(b) Request for such refund shall be processed administratively under such rules and regulations thereof as shall be prescribed by the city or its contractor. Refunds may be granted as herein authorized only upon the written approval of the city or its contractor.
(Code 1989, § 11-69; Ord. No. 187, § 21, 9-20-1982)
891:
Refuse collectors are instructed to remove only the contents of the refuse containers. It is possible, however, to have a small amount of extra yard waste removed on the regular day of service for an extra charge, providing this material is placed in carton boxes and left next to the refuse containers. The city or its contractor shall be notified by the customer before the day of collection. The city or its contractor will determine the charge according to the amount of material to be removed.
(Code 1989, § 11-70; Ord. No. 187, § 22, 9-20-1982)
892:
(a) No person shall deposit for curbside pick-up any garbage, hazardous waste, inert trash or yard waste not contained within proper containers or otherwise properly prepared for pick-up in accordance with the requirements of this chapter. In addition, it shall be the duty of each person depositing specialized waste at the curb side to first make arrangements with the city's designated contractor for the pick-up of such waste. Specialized waste includes yard waste that is too bulky for authorized containers, large limbs and trees, inert trash, and other items which are not part of the regular garbage collection service provided by the city.
(b) Any person failing to remove or cause the removal of specialized waste or any garbage, yard waste or inert trash not in proper containers or properly prepared for removal within seven days after a written warning notice from the city requesting such removal shall be in violation of this chapter. Any person who is convicted of a first offense under this section shall be subject to a fine of $50.00. Any person who is convicted of a second violation of this section shall be punished by a fine of $125.00. Any person who is convicted of a third or any subsequent violation of this section shall be punished by a fine of not less than $500.00, nor more than $1,000.00, and each day that a violation occurs or continues shall constitute a separate offense.
(c) In addition, in the event that the occupant, owner or other responsible party fails to remove or cause the removal within the time specified, the city shall have the right to remove or cause the removal of such items at the expense of the owner and occupant, and the expense shall be added to and become part of the owner or occupant's garbage bill. In the case of rental property, whether single-family or multifamily, the tenant and the owner shall be jointly and severally liable for the cost of removal. In the case of multifamily fee simple property, the owner-occupant and the homeowners' association, if any, shall be jointly and severally liable for the cost of removal. If there is no homeowners' association, the management company, if any, shall be jointly and severally liable with the owner-occupant for the cost of removal. In the event that any removal fee remains unpaid for a period of 30 days after written notice, the city may pursue any and all civil remedies available to the city at law or in equity to collect the fee, and the city may, after an additional 15-day period of prior written notice, discontinue water and garbage service to the applicable property. The punishment or conviction of any person under subsection (b) of this section shall not relieve the person from paying any unpaid removal fee; nor shall payment of any unpaid removal fee bar criminal prosecution for any violation of this chapter.
(Code 1989, § 11-71; Ord. No. 400, § 1, 2-16-1998)
894:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act, O.C.G.A. § 12-8-60 et seq.; transportation of biomedical waste, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-253.1.
895:
Commercial solid waste customers in the city are authorized to contract for commercial solid waste collection and disposal services from any contractor, provided that such contractor first obtains a solid waste collection permit from the city. Rates and other contract terms, including, but not limited to, container size and frequency of collections, shall be negotiated between the contractor and the customer, provided that such terms do not conflict with the provisions of this chapter or other applicable city ordinances.
(Code 1989, § 11-81; Ord. No. 354, § 1, 12-19-1994)
896:
It shall be unlawful for any commercial solid waste contractor (hereinafter "commercial contractor") to provide commercial solid waste collection and disposal services within the city without first obtaining a city solid waste collection permit. Contractors desiring to perform such services shall make written application to the city for a permit on forms prescribed by the city director of finance. All applications shall be accompanied by a $500.00 application fee to defray investigative, administrative and regulatory costs. Permits shall be issued to qualified applicants for the full calendar year, or for the number of months remaining in the calendar year, at the time the application is approved. Each commercial contractor issued a permit shall pay a quarterly permit fee to the city as provided in section 38-25. All permits granted under this chapter shall expire on December 31 of each year. Commercial contractors desiring to renew their permits shall file renewal applications accompanied by a $500.00 renewal application fee. The renewal application shall be submitted on forms prescribed by the director on or before November 15 of each year. In the event annual permit fees go unpaid after the due date, a ten percent penalty will be charged, based upon the past due amount. Further, a 12 percent per annum interest charge shall accrue until the permit fees are paid in full.
(Code 1989, § 11-82; Ord. No. 354, § 2, 12-19-1994; Ord. No. 421, § 1, 4-3-1999; Ord. No. 505, 9-23-2002)
897:
(a) Each commercial contractor shall pay a permit fee to be set by the city council from time to time per cubic yard of solid waste removed from the city, payable in accordance with billing and reporting procedures adopted from time to time by the director. For the purposes of determining the permit fee, solid waste shall be deemed to include trash, construction debris, demolition debris, medical waste, yard waste and rubbish, inert waste, hazardous waste, and any other solid waste not covered under separate contract with the city. In general, the volume and weights of solid waste shall be based upon actual weights of containers. Where actual weighing is not done, the permit fees shall be based upon the sizes of the containers, the frequency of collection and the types of waste mix in the container. The director will provide the average weight factors to be used. For the purpose of fee calculation, all containers shall be deemed full at the time of each collection. On or before the tenth working day of the first month following the end of each calendar quarter, the commercial contractor shall submit a quarterly fee based upon the cubic yards of waste removed from the city for the immediately preceding quarter, together with a report providing such information as the director shall deem appropriate. In the event permit fees go unpaid after the due date, a ten percent penalty will be charged based upon the past due amount. Further, a 12 percent per annum interest charge shall accrue until the permit fees are paid in full. The report shall contain, but shall not be limited to, a listing of customers served during the quarter, together with the size of containers and collection frequency for each customer; total tons of materials landfilled and recycled by city customers; identification of landfills used by the contractor; and identification of end users of recycled materials. The report shall be submitted in written form. The director or his designee shall have the right to examine at any time commercial contractors' books, records and computer data relating to the removal of solid waste from the city in order to verify or determine the amounts which should be remitted to the city. Each commercial contractor shall make its books, records and computer data pertinent to the removal of solid waste from the city available for audit. If the results of any such audit show that any of the commercial contractor's reports understate the amount owing to the city, the underpayment shall be remitted to the city immediately, and if the understatement amounts to five percent or more, the commercial contractor shall also remit to the city a sum equal to ten percent of the underpayment, and shall also reimburse the city for its costs in conducting the audit.
(b) All permitted commercial contractors shall also submit such other reports as the director may reasonably require regarding the removal of solid waste from the city in order to provide information needed by the city to comply with applicable state and federal reporting requirements imposed upon the city. Solid waste refers to trash and to recycling, if the permitted hauler provides recycling services. All permitted commercial contractors shall provide quarterly information regarding tons landfilled and recycled to their city customers that are legally required to reduce their landfilled solid waste by 25 percent. This information shall be provided in a timely and accurate manner. Withholding of this information, delay in providing the information which causes the city customer to miss a legal deadline, or the providing of inaccurate information shall constitute a violation of this chapter and may result in fines, permit revocation, or both, as provided in sections 38-30 and 38-31.
(c) Every permitted commercial contractor is required to provide dependable solid waste service to customers within the city. Failure to provide dependable service may result in fines, permit revocation, or both, as provided in sections 38-30 and 38-31.
(Code 1989, § 11-83; Ord. No. 354, § 3, 12-19-1994; Ord. No. 421, § 2, 5-3-1999; Ord. No. 455, § 1, 11-6-2000; Ord. No. 505, 9-23-2002)
898:
An adequate number of vehicles shall be provided by the commercial contractor to service its city customers. All such vehicles shall be licensed in the state and shall operate in compliance with all applicable state, federal and municipal regulations. All vehicles and other equipment shall be kept in proper repair and sanitary condition. Each vehicle shall have at least one broom and shovel to clean up solid waste that may be spilled or otherwise scattered during the process of collection. All vehicles shall be sufficiently secure so as to prevent any littering of solid waste and/or leakage of fluid. No vehicle shall be willfully overloaded. Each vehicle shall be operated by a qualified driver holding a valid license of the category required to operate such vehicles.
(Code 1989, § 11-84; Ord. No. 354, § 4, 12-19-1994)
899:
(a) Each commercial contractor shall provide and maintain, during the term of its permit, public liability and property damage insurance and umbrella coverage in such amounts as shall be reasonably determined from time to time by the director. The initial insurance requirements are as follows:
(1) Public liability:
a. $500,000.00 per person.
b. $1,000,000.00 per accident.
(2) Property damage: $500,000.00 per any one claim.
(3) Performance bond: varies according to number of city contracts.
(b) Each commercial contractor shall provide a certificate of such insurance to the city prior to undertaking collection services within the city, and, at each annual renewal of the permit, shall submit to the city an updated certificate of insurance together with the annual permit fee. Each commercial contractor shall defend, indemnify and save harmless and protect the city, its officers and agents, from any and all liability, loss or claims, actions, demands or judgments made against it for loss, damage or personal injury sustained by any person or entity whatsoever in connection with the services rendered by the commercial contractor, unless such damages are due to the negligence of the city, its officers, agents or employees.
(Code 1989, § 11-85; Ord. No. 354, § 5, 12-19-1994; Ord. No. 421, § 3, 5-3-1999)
900:
Each commercial contractor shall have a positive net worth and adequate capital and assets to perform its contracts with city customers. As a condition to the issuance of a permit, the director may require the submission of financial statements or similar information to verify these financial requirements. Any information submitted that is proprietary or constitutes a trade secret shall, subject to applicable law, be held confidential by the city.
(Code 1989, § 11-86; Ord. No. 354, § 6, 12-19-1994)
901:
Not less than ten days prior to commencing service, each commercial contractor shall furnish for the city's approval the initial schedules and maps of all routes to be used in servicing the commercial contractor's city customers. Any charges in routes and/or schedules shall also be subject to the director's approval, which will not be unreasonably withheld. The commercial contractor shall only undertake collections during the city's normal hours of collection, as adopted from time to time by the director. Exceptions may be made only upon the mutual agreement of the director and the commercial contractor. The commercial contractor shall also comply with all applicable city ordinances, including the city's noise provisions.
(Code 1989, § 11-87; Ord. No. 354, § 7, 12-19-1994)
902:
Any violation of this chapter by the commercial contractor may be punished according to the penalties described in section 1-8. Each day that a violation occurs shall constitute a separate offense. The city shall also have the right to initiate civil action to compel compliance with this chapter and to collect any unpaid permit fees.
(Code 1989, § 11-88; Ord. No. 354, § 8, 12-19-1994)
903:
If a commercial contractor fails to perform in accordance with this chapter or other applicable ordinances, the director shall have the right to demand, in writing, adequate assurance from the commercial contractor that steps have been taken to rectify the situation. The commercial contractor must, within seven days of receipt of such demand, return to the director a written statement that explains reasons for non-performance or delayed, partial or substandard performance, and provides adequate assurance as to future performance. In the event that the commercial contractor fails to submit a statement satisfactory to the director, the director may revoke the commercial contractor's permit. Such revocation shall become effective 30 days following a notice of revocation to the commercial contractor. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, the right to continue to operate under a permit issued by the city is expressly conditioned upon the commercial contractor's timely payment of permit fees. Continued operation in the city without payment of such fees shall be unlawful. In addition, the city may revoke a permit for nonpayment of fees immediately and without notice.
(Code 1989, § 11-89; Ord. No. 354, § 9, 12-19-1994)
904:
(a) It is the policy and intent of the city that commercial and industrial refuse collection services are provided within the city on a competitive, free market basis. In order to promote this policy and intent, commercial and industrial customers within the city are encouraged to solicit multiple bids from qualified vendors for the provision of refuse collection services.
(b) In furtherance of this policy and intent, qualified vendors are encouraged to solicit commercial and industrial customers within the city for the purpose of providing commercial and industrial refuse collection services. It is also the policy and intent of the city that all qualified commercial and industrial vendors have free access to the market within the city, that all such vendors are afforded an equal opportunity to complete for and provide such services, and that no vendor shall be given preference over another.
(Code 1989, § 11-90; Res. No. 536, §§ 1, 2, 6-13-1994)
906:
Footnote 2:
State Law reference— Georgia Comprehensive Solid Waste Management Act, O.C.G.A. § 12-8-20 et seq.
908:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Director means the city director of community development or his designee.
Land disturbance permit means a permit issued by the city authorizing development activity, which permit requires the submission of development plans for review and approval by the community development department.
Plan applicant means any person or entity required to submit plans and apply for a land disturbance permit as a condition to development of a project within the city.
(Code 1989, § 11-101; Ord. No. 412, § 2, 9-21-1998; Ord. No. 498, § I, 7-15-2002)
909:
(a) Each plan applicant shall, as a condition of undertaking development activity within the city, submit a waste generation analysis and reduction plan (WGA) as part of and in conjunction with the submission of development plans to the community development department. The waste generation analysis and reduction plan shall contain such information as is specified in this chapter and shall be designed to establish a 25 percent reduction in the anticipated solid waste to be generated by the project. No land disturbance permit shall be issued or approved by the community development department unless and until the plan contains an approved WGA.
(b) Each WGA shall be set forth in writing and shall contain, but not be limited to, the following:
(1) The full name of the person applying for WGA approval.
(2) The name and size of the proposed project.
(3) The types of waste that will be generated at the site.
(4) Annual projected tons of waste.
(5) Plans and strategies for achieving a 25 percent solid waste reduction.
(6) Plans for notifying and assuring tenant compliance with the provisions of the WGA.
(7) A list of specific items to be recycled and the anticipated tons of annual reduction.
(8) A list of the size of containers and the frequency of pick-ups to be used for solid waste pick-up and recycling.
(9) A description of design features to be utilized to accommodate waste reduction practices and solid waste collection.
(10) Such other information as the director may reasonably require.
(c) In order to develop the WGA, the plan applicant shall utilize the solid waste generation rates established by the National Solid Waste Management Association and the Atlanta Regional Commission, or generation rates as approved by the director.
(Code 1989, § 11-102; Ord. No. 412, § 3, 9-21-1998; Ord. No. 498, § I, 7-15-2002)
910:
Following the approval of a WGA, the issuance of a land disturbance permit and the completion of the project, the applicant or project owner shall thereafter submit to the director reports reflecting compliance with the approved WGA. Failure to maintain compliance with the required 25 percent waste reduction shall be a violation of this chapter and may result in non-renewal of any permits or licenses granted by the city to conduct business. Proof of compliance with this chapter is required for a business license renewal.
(Code 1989, § 11-103; Ord. No. 412, § 4, 9-21-1998; Ord. No. 498, § I, 7-15-2002)
911:
For the purposes of carrying out the provisions of this chapter, the director may enter upon any public or private land in a reasonable and lawful manner during normal business hours for purposes of sampling, inspection and observation. Failure to provide reasonable access shall constitute a violation of this chapter.
(Code 1989, § 11-104; Ord. No. 412, § 5, 9-21-1998; Ord. No. 498, § I, 7-15-2002)
912:
Any person, firm or corporation violating any provision of this chapter shall be fined according to the penalties described in section 1-8 for each offense, and each day that the offense occurs shall be considered a separate and distinct offense. Any violation of this chapter is hereby declared to be a nuisance, and in addition to any other relief provided in this chapter, the city attorney may apply to a court of competent jurisdiction for an injunction to prohibit the continuation of any such violation of this chapter. Such application for relief may include seeking a temporary restraining order, temporary injunction and permanent injunction. Cases involving violations of this chapter may also be heard by the code enforcement board for the purpose of levying fines.
(Code 1989, § 11-105; Ord. No. 412, § 6, 9-21-1998; Ord. No. 498, § I, 7-15-2002)

916:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any land owner, or the tenant of any land owner, to erect any fence or other device that obstructs the clear view of any adjacent land owner from entering or exiting any street in the city.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any land owner, or the tenant of any land owner, to grow or maintain any hedge that obstructs the clear view of the entrance or exit of any adjacent land owner from entering or exiting any street in the city.
(Code 1989, § 17-1; Ord. No. 123, § 1, 10-23-1972)
919:
The city council does hereby establish for the city, districts to be known as "street lighting districts." Such districts shall be classified according to the local area roads and streets, as follows:
(1) Major thoroughfare districts.
(2) Industrial parkway districts.
(3) Collector street districts.
(4) Local and residential street districts.
(Code 1989, § 17-20; Ord. No. 176, § 1, 3-10-1980)
920:
The official zoning map for the city shall be utilized for the purpose of demonstrating the street lighting districts, and the office of the city public works department shall establish records designating these various street lighting districts throughout the city to which reference can be made for a full and complete description of each district.
(Code 1989, § 17-21; Ord. No. 176, § 2, 3-10-1980)
921:
In areas where special conditions as to safety, security, land topography, economic and other factors may be involved, the city council may create special street lighting districts and provide for special street lighting under such terms and conditions as may be determined by the city council, any other provisions of this article to the contrary notwithstanding; provided, however, that in such instances, a public hearing shall be held by the city council after advertisement in the official organ of the city one time at least ten days before conducting such public hearing.
(Code 1989, § 17-22; Ord. No. 176, § 14, 3-10-1980)
922:
Real estate developers, whether single-family or multifamily residential, commercial, office-institutional, industrial or community unit plan, shall, prior to the receipt of any building permit for their developments, provide the city with detailed site plans of the streets to be used in their developments and showing the location of all street lights; submit proof of payment for pole and electrical installation; and shall comply in every respect with the provisions of this article.
(Code 1989, § 17-23; Ord. No. 176, § 3, 3-10-1980)
923:
Property owners residing in the city and desiring street lighting for the area in which they live, may petition the city public works department to have such service. Such petition must contain not less than ten property owners representing not less than 65 percent of the property owners within the district to be established. A petition may be brought by less than ten property owners where such petitioners represent 100 percent of the property owners within the district to be established.
(Code 1989, § 17-24; Ord. No. 176, § 4, 3-10-1980)
924:
After investigation by the public works department as to advisability of establishing such a district, the petition shall be presented to the city council for consideration upon a public hearing. After the public hearing, the petition will be either approved or disapproved by the city council.
(Code 1989, § 17-25; Ord. No. 176, § 5, 3-10-1980)
925:
Street lighting in districts other than single-family residential shall be permitted only with the approval of the city building official, subject to the safety, economic and other factors involved, and only upon final approval by the city council, and upon compliance with the standards hereinafter provided.
(Code 1989, § 17-26; Ord. No. 176, § 12, 3-10-1980)
926:
(a) In those districts now in existence or which may hereafter be created in which there is construction cost, the same shall be retired as per agreement or contract with the public utility or other person to whom the indebtedness is owed and shall be billed accordingly per lot.
(b) The term "lot" is hereby defined as any single tract of land which falls within any of the zoning classifications as defined by the zoning ordinance.
(c) In areas zoned for purposes other than single-family residential, different criteria may be adopted by the city council for the payment of energy cost and retirement of construction cost.
(Code 1989, § 17-27; Ord. No. 176, §§ 7, 8, 3-10-1980)
927:
The cost of service for creation of street lighting districts created shall be a service cost and not a tax, as such service is authorized by article IX, section 4, paragraph 2 of the 1983 constitution of the state.
(Code 1989, § 17-28; Ord. No. 176, § 6, 3-10-1980)
928:
The cost of providing and maintaining the service in existing street lighting districts, and in street lighting districts hereafter created, shall be borne by those citizens and residents receiving the service. The charge therefor shall be the actual cost of the energy, plus the pro-rata share of the retirement of any construction cost, plus ten percent for administrative cost.
(Code 1989, § 17-29; Ord. No. 176, § 7, 3-10-1980)
929:
The due date for the payment of the services and sums herein provided for shall be the same date of each month as water bills are due to the city and subject to the same penalties for late payment and for failure to pay. Any service provided by the city may be discontinued for late payment or nonpayment, as herein provided for.
(Code 1989, § 17-30; Ord. No. 176, § 9, 3-10-1980)
930:
The billing, accounting, collecting, and receiving of moneys herein provided for is hereby declared to be the responsibility of the city clerk.
(Code 1989, § 17-31; Ord. No. 176, § 10, 3-10-1980)
931:
The owner, developer or other person developing a subdivision, or any other property, shall provide street lighting services to conform to all of the standards herein provided for, and in addition thereto, shall be required to obtain a permit from community development prior to commencing any construction of any street lighting facilities, and the city shall not accept any public streets or roads proposed to be dedicated until such time as the provisions hereof have been complied with.
(Code 1989, § 17-32; Ord. No. 176, § 11, 3-10-1980)
932:
Street lights shall be required to be provided by the developers of all new subdivisions or other projects within the city unless waived by the city council at a regular meeting. Unless so waived, the preliminary plat of the subdivision or other development shall make provisions for street lights. At the time of and as a requirement of the submission of a final plat, unless waived by the city council as herein provided, the developer shall:
(1) Submit a drawing of the subdivision's or development's layout showing location of street lights. The drawing must be approved by the city building official prior to obtaining any building permit within that subdivision or development. Such layout may be shown on the final plat. Fixtures and standards/poles installed or used shall be approved by the utility company which will be responsible for the maintenance of the facilities and by the city. The fixtures shall be mounted above the ground and shall have appropriate arm length to place the light over the street. No arm shall be less than 2½ feet long. Post-top luminaries may be permitted when approved by the city building official. Post-top luminary fixtures shall be located not more than 200 feet apart, and at least one light shall be located at each street intersection within the subdivision or development.
(2) Pay all costs for standards/poles, fixtures and any other related items or materials necessary for the installation.
(3) Submit proof of payment for complete installation to the city building official.
(4) Submit a copy of an executed agreement with the utility company for complete maintenance of all installations.
(Code 1989, § 17-33; Ord. No. 176, § 20, 3-10-1980)
933:
In subdivisions or other developments utilizing underground cable for electrical service, the developers shall be required to accomplish the same items listed in other sections hereof.
(Code 1989, § 17-34; Ord. No. 176, § 21, 3-10-1980)
